subject.title: Feature Request: config:pre-apply hook for validating config changes

question: Should OpenClaw add a synchronous plugin/API config-write veto hook, and what redaction, trust, timeout, recursion, ordering, and failure semantics should it have across RPC and shared mutation paths?
rationale: Source inspection proves the seam is missing, but a hook that can inspect and block persisted config changes is a new security-sensitive plugin API contract that code review cannot choose safely without maintainer intent.

options.title: Design guarded config-write hook
options.body: Add a narrow, documented pre-persistence hook covering config.set, config.patch, config.apply, and shared mutation helpers with explicit redaction, timeout, recursion, ordering, and rejection semantics.

options.title: Limit to built-in validation
options.body: Keep config validation, SecretRef preflight, and agent-write allowlists in core, and document external validators as optional helpers that cannot enforce mandatory pre-apply policy.

options.title: Fold into broader preflight design
options.body: Defer this specific hook until the related preflight/config validation direction chooses one shared validation contract across startup and config mutation.

recommendation.title: Design guarded config-write hook
recommendation.body: Add a narrow, documented pre-persistence hook covering config.set, config.patch, config.apply, and shared mutation helpers with explicit redaction, timeout, recursion, ordering, and rejection semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: They already framed this issue as an unresolved config validation/mutation product boundary and have adjacent gateway config/security history.
